Jordan — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a compact workbook that shows baseline hosted API rates and a couple of residency scenarios. High level answers below, then I included a short note on recommended committed tiers.

Key numbers (summary):
- Baseline hosted API (US region): $0.60 per 1k prompt tokens, $0.80 per 1k completion tokens (example model family).
- EU residency adder (option A): $1,200/month managed residency fee for dedicated EU tenancy (covers EU-only logging/audit config + KMS integration).
- EU residency adder (option B): usage-based adder of $0.10 per 1k tokens routed to EU-hosted instances (applies only for cross-region routing scenarios).
- Committed volume discounts: 5% for annual 5M token commit, 12% for 20M+ commit (can layer with residency adder unless customer wants a single-shape enterprise quote).

I've attached: redwood-transatlantic-ratecard-2025.xlsx (compact scenarios) and a short residency note. Would you like me to put together a one-page proposal with a recommended path (pilot -> commit) and an example 12-month TCO for 5M tokens/month?

Proposed next step: 30-minute walkthrough next week to align assumptions. I'm free Tue/Wed morning PT.

Best,

Fwding Jordan's ask and the draft numbers I proposed (attached). Two quick internal Qs before I send a proposal:

1) Residency adder: Option A ($1,200/mo managed residency) vs Option B (usage add-on $0.10/1k). For a mid-sized pilot (5M tokens/mo) which is more defensible from an ops/cost standpoint? My read: Option A simplifies compliance and gives predictable cost to procurement, but Option B can be more attractive if we need to keep sticker low for first 3 months. Thoughts?

2) Discounting flexibility: Jordan asked about committed discounts. He referenced internal infra TCO — can we offer 8% for an annual 5M commit (instead of public 5%) if we add a 6-month pilot at a reduced residency fee (waive first 2 months)? I want margin but we need a competitive hook.

Marking for Rishi for pricing approval and Marissa for AE playbook input.

Thanks — Camila

Hi Jordan and Lina — thanks for the patience. Following internal alignment, here's a concise answer you can use in procurement pack and share with your GDPR team if helpful. I've attached a one-page PDF proposal for Acme with the numbers below.

Finalized numbers (hosted API, model family = Redwood-L1-equivalent):
- Baseline (US region): $0.60 / 1k prompt tokens, $0.80 / 1k completion tokens.
- EU residency options (choose one):
  • Managed residency (Option A): $1,000 / month (we adjusted to be competitive) — includes EU-only logging partition, KMS integration, and quarterly audit report.
  • Usage adder (Option B): $0.08 / 1k tokens routed to EU-hosted instances.
- Committed volume: 5% standard discount for 5M tokens/month annual commit. For Acme we can offer 8% if they commit to 5M tokens/month for 12 months and accept a 6-month pilot with the first two months of the residency fee waived.
- Minimum term: pilot can be month-to-month for first 3 months; committed term begins at month 4 if they sign.

Example TCO (illustrative):
- 5M tokens/month (prompt+completion mix as in attached sheet) -> ~ $18,000/month baseline before discounts. With 8% committed discount + managed residency = ~$16,560/month.

Attachments: acme-proposal-v1.pdf (contains the worked examples and contract bullets); redwood-transatlantic-ratecard-2025.xlsx (raw math).

- Jordan: confirm whether Acme prefers managed residency or usage adder for the pilot.
- Lina: if you want, I can include the SOC2 summary and sample audit scopes in the next package.
